name: Seven Piece African Drum Set
description:
# Seven Piece African Drum Set

\\nSeven Piece African Drum Set has enough instruments for sevens musicians to all play at once. With a Kenkeni, Sangban, three djembes, a gankogui and shekere you will have that full African groove and sound. Items pictures are an example of what your instruments will look like. \\n \\nWhat you get: \\n \\n**_Ghanaian Djembe_** \\n \\nA light wood drum with a small head but an impressive bass, tone, slap definition for its size. A great drum for children, travelers, or adults wanting an affordable first Djembe with an authentic African sound. \\n \\n**_Sangban_** \\n \\nThe Sangban is the middle size drum of the dundun set and often plays the defining phase of a rhythm.  This drum can be either a soft or hard wood depending on the tone and projection required. These drums are fitted with Australian cow hide on both sides using top quality marine rope. These drums are made to order and you have the option to choose your own rope and fabric colours to complete your individual design. \\n \\n_**Kenkeni**_ \\n \\nThe Kenkenni is the smallest size drum of the dundun set, is the timekeeper and completes the melody of the rhythm.  This drum can be either a soft or hard wood depending on the tone and projection required. The Kenkeni are fitted with Australian cow hide on both sides using top quality marine rope. These Kenkeni are made to order and you have the option to choose your own rope and fabric colours to complete your individual design. \\n \\n**_Gankogui_** \\n \\nThe double bell gankogui is a hand-forged iron bell. One gankogui actually consists of two bells, the smaller, higher-pitched one resting atop the larger, lower one.  Many Eve ensembles include two gankoguiwo, one much bigger than the other. \\n \\n**_Shekere_** \\n \\nThe **shekere** is an instrument from West Africa consisting of a dried gourd with beads woven into a net covering the gourd. Throughout the continent there are similar gourd/bead or gourd/seed percussion instruments. Some are the _lilolo_, _axatse_ ([Ghana](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana "Ghana")), _djabara_ ([Guinea](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guinea "Guinea")), _ushàkà_, and _chequere_. It is predominantly called _shekere_ in [Nigeria](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigeria "Nigeria"). \\n \\n_**Items pictures are an example of what your instruments look like. We custom make your order and make every effort to match the colours of your school. Let us know if you have specific colours in mind!**_ \\n \\n**_NB: Please note this order is too large to send via online shipping. Please contact us to organise shipping._**
